Example: 𝒜^N with a coordinatewise 𝒜-valued inner product is a Hilbert 𝒜-module. The type is Mathlib `WithCStarModule 𝒜 (Fin N -> 𝒜)`, notation C-star-mod(𝒜, Fin N -> 𝒜), the same type synonym 32I is rendered on and the one 36III `selfDual_pi` (TowardsVN.lean:666) and 33I use as their witness; completeness, the Hilbert as opposed to pre-Hilbert half, is the CompleteSpace instance the synonym carries at a complete 𝒜. DIFFERS ON THE DISPLAYED FORMULA, and only there. Mathlib builds the inner product on a Pi type coordinatewise (Analysis/CStarAlgebra/Module/Constructions.lean:235, inner x y = sum over i of inner (x i) (y i)) out of the inner product of 𝒜 over itself, which is `inner x y := y * star x` (ibid.:79, `WithCStarModule.inner_def` at ibid.:91). So our 𝒜^N carries inner x y = sum over n of (y n) * star (x n) where 32II displays sum over n of star (x n) * (y n) -- the two factors in the other order. Both satisfy every clause of 32I -- for Mathlib's, inner x (a * y) = (a y) star x = a * inner x y, so it too is additive and 𝒜-linear in the second argument with the scalar on the left, and it is positive on the diagonal and star-symmetric, and the two are each other read in the opposite algebra, so they agree exactly when 𝒜 is commutative and not otherwise. The same mismatch is recorded one row down at 32IV, where it is harmless because C[0,1] is commutative; here 𝒜 is arbitrary, so it is not.
